slides.1.title: The Three Douro Sub-regions in Detail
slides.1.html:
1️⃣ Baixo Corgo

  • Closest to the ocean (80km from Porto), with a mild Atlantic influence
  • Relatively high annual rainfall (700–900mm) and a cooler climate
  • Mainly produces basic Port and everyday Douro table wine
  • Well-known producers: Ferreira・Ramos Pinto

2️⃣ Cima Corgo ⭐ The heart of the region

  • The core of the Douro and the main source of top Vintage Port
  • Annual rainfall of 500–700mm, with a pronounced continental climate
  • Densely packed with famous estates (Quintas): Quinta do Crasto・Quinta do Vale Meão・Niepoort
  • The most spectacular schist terraces, and the heart of the UNESCO World Heritage area

3️⃣ Douro Superior

  • Furthest inland with the most extreme climate: the hottest summers (up to 40°C) and the coldest winters
  • Lowest annual rainfall (400–500mm), almost semi-arid
  • Flatter and the most mechanised, with the greatest potential as an emerging area
  • Main grapes: Touriga Nacional・Touriga Franca ripen perfectly here
slides.2.title: The Rise of Unfortified Douro Red Wines
slides.2.html:
In the early 21st century, a group of pioneering winemakers such as the "Douro Boys" launched a revolution in unfortified dry red wines from the Douro.

🌟 Characteristics of top Douro reds

  • Built around Touriga Nacional, blended with Touriga Franca・Tinta Barroca and others
  • Dark and complex, with floral notes (violet・rose), minerality and spice
  • Suited to ageing for 10–20 years and comparable with the world's top red wines

🍷 Representative wines

  • Barca Velha (Ferreirinha): Portugal's most iconic top red wine
  • Quinta do Crasto Reserva: internationally known and good value
  • Niepoort Redoma: a leading organic, natural-style wine

Young vines in Douro Superior are also beginning to produce quality wines, making it an emerging area to watch.
